projects.title: Campsite Reservation API v1 (RESTful)
projects.description:
A RESTful API written as the capstone project for the course CS 493: Cloud Application Development at Oregon State University.

This API is intended to be a representation of a system that might be used to reserve a campsite at a particular campground. 
The database for this API consists of three entities: Site, Reservation, and User. The Site entity represents a campsite which has an id, number, size, type, and a reservation if one exists. The Site number would be the number used to identify the physical campsite within the campground, such as A1, D4, C23, etc. The size field represents the dimensions of the site (i.e., “10 x 12”) and the type field represents the type of campsite (i.e., tent, RV). 
The Reservation entity represents a reservation made by a user for a particular Site. It contains the following fields: an id, arrival_date, departure_date, paid_in_full, site and reserved_by. The arrival_date and departure_date are strings which should be a representation of their respective dates. In practice, I would intend this to be the output of the Date constructor’s toJSON() method. Paid_in_full is a Boolean which indicates whether the user has paid all that is due to use the Site. The site field contains the id for the Site which is being reserved, however, the JSON output will contain a link to the site. Finally, the reserved_by field holds the username of the User that made the reservation. Similar to the site field, the JSON response will contain a link to the User.
The User entity represents a user of the system. The entity contains fields for the user’s id, first_name, last_name, username, and an array of Reservation. Each item of the Reservation array will be a link to the Reservation itself.

projects.title: Foliospace
projects.description:
Program capstone project completed in collaboration with Andrea Dias (Github: @andreadias) and Arthur Liou (Github: @artliou).

General overview: The application is a portfolio website builder. Users will be able to build and customize various components of their website to present a clean and professional portfolio to showcase for prospective employers. The portfolio can be configured to display the user’s projects, such as title, artwork/images, links (to Github / LinkedIn), descriptions and other text. 

Technologies used:
-> APIs: Okta, Cloudinary, AWS/JawsDB MySQL
-> Front-End: Javascript, React, Bootstrap, Pug, Babel
-> Server: Node.js, Express/Express-Session, DotEnv, Concurrently
-> Database: MySQL, JawsDB MySQL, AWS
-> Deployment: Heroku, JawsDB MySQL
-> Dev Tools: Visual Studio Code, Sequel Pro / Navicat, NPM

My contributions:
-> Server, server-side routes / processes for CRUD operations for /projects, /portfolio, and file uploads.
-> Dashboard, Project setup, and Projects list views (.pug) and functionalities
-> Integration of Cloudinary storage and upload widget
